# Plain C# twins for the read and modify tasks

- **Status:** Done 2026-10-27 (C# twins for tasks 004, 005, 007, 008 with starting code and existing_code_tokens; gate 238 + 71; review D44)
- **Shape:** Story
- **Type:** feature (thin slice; a benchmark arm needs its own Decider record and old rows stay labeled)
- **Milestone:** Measure first: does Phrase beat plain C# on tokens and attempts?
- **Source:** Second thin-slice cut of old card 086 (2026-10-27): building eight C# twins and a runner is more than one run. Cards 086, 095 and 096 are serial (they share the bench/csharp-baseline tree), and the N=5 run is card 094. Pre-registered bar: Decider D32.
- **Depends on:** 086
- **Story:** As Riley, I want C# twins of the four read and modify development tasks (004, 005, 007, 008) with xUnit outcome checks identical in meaning to their Phrase tasks, so that the change tasks are measured on the same footing in plain C#, and the context needed to change existing code is counted.
- **Acceptance criteria (Given/When/Then; at most 3, each failing on partial work):**
  1. Given tasks 004, 005, 007 and 008, When the C# suite is listed, Then each has a C# prompt with the starting C# code equivalent to its Phrase starting code, and an xUnit outcome check that tests the same observable outcome as its Phrase twin (the check fails if the outcome set differs)
  2. Given a recorded correct C# reply for each task, When the runner scores it, Then it passes, and a recorded wrong reply fails with the failing test named
  3. Given the change tasks, When a row is stored, Then it records kind change and the tokens of the existing code the model had to read (the context needed to change existing code)

## Context

- Change tasks are where Phrase is claimed to help most; counting the existing-code context tokens answers the assessment's point that writing new code is not the only cost.
- Files: a new bench/csharp-baseline tree and its own runner; it does not edit tools/Phrase.Bench. Twins are neutral: each C# task is the same observable outcome as its Phrase task, uses the same libraries (FastEndpoints only when the outcome is an HTTP endpoint), the prompt contains no Phrase documentation, and each task is judged by xUnit tests (specs as tests), the fair baseline.
- Safety rules apply in full. The sealed holdouts (bench/holdout-hashes.txt) are not read.
